This is a suit for decree of possession, recovery of mesne profits and damages filed by the plaintiff against the defendant.
During the trial of the present case, the defendant expired on 13.06.2013.

Thereafter, vide order dated 02.04.2014, his LRs were impleaded in the array of parties.
2.

Succinctly put, the case of plaintiff, as per plaint is that he is the absolute owner of property bearing no. B-252, Sudershan Park, New Delhi - 110015 (previously WZ-73/1, old plot no. 36, part of khasra no. 27/44/616, RE of village Basai Darapur), measuring 100 sq yards [hereinafter referred as 'suit property'].
His father late Sh. Teja Singh was the owner of half undivided share of built-up property no. WZ-73/1, old plot no. 36, measuring 200 sq yards by virtue of registered sale deed dated 01.03.1956.
He died on 16.06.1998.
His mother late Smt. Gian Kaur had pre-deceased his father and died on 02.09.1994.
His father was survived by him (plaintiff) and four daughters.

His sisters relinquished their shares in the suit property in his favour vide registered relinquishment deed dated 24.11.2008.
3.

It has been further submitted that the defendant was not having any place or shelter to live in and in the year 1983, he pleaded with Digitally signed by NAVEEN NAVEEN GUPTA GUPTA Date:
2026.04.01 16:32:58 +0530 father of plaintiff to allow him to stay in the suit property without consideration.

He (defendant) promised to leave as and when alternate arrangements were made by him or father of plaintiff required him to do so.
Thereafter, father of plaintiff, who was also the maternal uncle of defendant, allowed him (defendant) to use a room, kitchen and bath/toilet in the said property.
A boundary wall had also been constructed at the suit property for safety.
After the death of his father in the year 1998, the suit property was owned by the plaintiff.

He,
out of family ties, allowed the defendant to attend his family responsibilities like education of his children without charging any license fee, but subject to payment of electricity and water charges.
4. It has been further averred that the plaintiff was regularly visiting the suit property during the lifetime of his father and also after his death.
He used to reside at the suit property as well.

The plaintiff was crestfallen to have noticed that the defendant without his consent and knowledge,
started raising construction over the suit property, which was reported to police station Moti Nagar on 29.03.2012.
At that time, the defendant claimed that he was interested in buying the suit property.
But, the plaintiff did not agree to the said proposal.
At that time, the defendant assured that he would demolish the said construction and vacate the premises by the end of May 2012.
The plaintiff when visited the suit property later on, he found that the defendant had illegally constructed two rooms with slab.

The plaintiff due to intervention of relatives and friends, had reserved actions against the defendant and his wife for this illegal activity, but moved both the authorities to convert the electricity and water connections in his (plaintiff) name.
6. It has been further averred that the status of defendant in the suit property was that of mere licensee.

Since the plaintiff was no longer interested in continuing him as licensee, he through legal notice dated 15.06.2012, terminated his license with immediate effect and called upon him to vacate and hand over peaceful and vacant possession of the said premises on or before 30.06.2012.

Further, the defendant was liable to pay damages for use and occupation of the suit premises @
Rs.25,000/- per month, keeping in view the present market rate of rent of the property, w.e.f.
01.07.2012.
The said notice was duly served upon the defendant, but he did not comply with the same.
Thus, the plaintiff has filed the present case praying for decree of possession of the suit property and recovery of Rs.25,000/- per month on account of damages.
7. In his written statement, the defendant has raised preliminary objections that the present suit is time barred.
He is the absolute and exclusive owner of the suit property.

He has further submitted that in the year 1956, one plot of 200 sq yards was purchased by one Dalip Singh and late Sh. Teja Singh in Rs.900/- and the suit property was half equal portion of the said plot.

Remaining half equal share was with late Sh. Teja Singh.
On 20.10.1984, late Sh. Teja Singh approached the defendant to sell the suit property.

He (defendant) told him that after five days, he would arrange money for him, as he (Sh. Teja Singh) had an urgent requirement of money to run some business and to purchase some property in Yamuna Nagar,
Haryana.
On 25.10.1984, late Sh. Teja Singh got agreed to sell the suit property in Rs.18,000/- and took Rs.3,000/- in advance from the defendant.
The last date of execution of the documents of the suit property was 25.11.1984.
However, the possession of the suit property was handed over to the defendant and his family members on 25.10.1984.
Unfortunately, there were communal riots in Delhi as well as in other sates.
Late Sh. Teja Singh went to Punjab to save his life and that of his family members and accordingly, could not come to execute the documents in favour of defendant.

It was only on 05.03.1986, late Sh. Teja Singh took Rs.15,000/- from defendant and executed the documents of suit property in his favour i.e. General Power of Attorney, Agreement to Sell, Affidavit and Receipt.
The said documents were duly signed by late Sh. Teja Singh, defendant and the eye witnesses.

They attempted to dispossess the defendant from the suit property and threw his goods and articles from the house.

Further, on 23.12.2012 at about 08:00 PM, the plaintiff and his family members came at the house of defendant and threatened to cause death and grievous hurt and to take possession of the suit property from the defendant with the help of anti- social elements.
Thereafter, Smt. Amrit Kaur and her son Parminder Singh gave written complaints to the worthy Commissioner of Police, Delhi, DCP West and SHO PS Moti Nagar.
But, no case was registered in this regard.
Subsequently, wife of defendant Smt. Amrit Kaur filed a complaint case before Ld. MM, Delhi.
The present case was the counter-blast of the said criminal case filed by wife of the defendant.
The plaintiff has filed the present case to extort money from the defendant.
9. On merits, the defendant has reiterated the submissions earlier made by him in the preliminary objections.
He has further stated that father of defendant was the real brother of late Sh. Teja Singh.
Further, he (defendant) had made boundary wall himself with his money and constructed three rooms, one laterine/bathroom and kitchen.
He had paid all the bills of water, telephone and electricity since after 05.03.1986.
Further, since he was the owner and in possession of the suit property since 05.03.1986, the plaintiff had no power to stop him from doing any construction in the suit property.
Only to show false cause of action, the wrong date [i.e. of 29.03.2012] had been made by the plaintiff in this case.

He (plaintiff) has come to know through the information sought under RTI Act that the defendant had created different title documents at different stages.

He (defendant) had submitted unregistered forged General Power of Attorney dated 23.09.2000 alleged to have been executed by plaintiff in favour of defendant with respect to 25 sq yards out of total area measuring 75 sq yards with address of the suit property, before the property tax department in North Delhi Municipal Corporation.
He had also submitted an unregistered title document dated 07.05.1997 before Tata Power Delhi Distribution Limited.
He had also filed different forged unregistered title documents dated 05.03.1986 [of suit property] alongwith written statement.

Final arguments were heard from Ld. Counsels for the parties.
Record has been perused.

Ld.
Counsel for the plaintiff has argued that the suit property originally belonged to the father of plaintiff.
The said fact was not disputed by the defendant in his written statement.
After the demise of late Sh. Teja Singh, the suit property devolved upon his legal heirs.
Later on, vide relinquishment deed dated 24.11.2008, sisters of the plaintiff relinquished their share in the suit property to the plaintiff and thereby, he became its absolute owner.
Ld. Counsel has further argued that the defendant prepared false transfer documents dated 05.03.1986 in respect of the suit property.

But,
evidence led by the plaintiff shows that the said documents were never executed by the father of plaintiff in favour of the defendant.
This could be inferred from the testimonies of PW-3 and PW-4.

Further, even the conclusion arrived at by the investigating agency pursuant to the investigation carried out after registration of FIR No. 250/2017 PS Moti Nagar proves that the defendant had prepared false transfer documents of the suit property.
Further, the admissions made by DW-1 in his testimony themselves demolished the case of defendant.
DW-1 admitted that the electricity meter stood in the name of plaintiff.
The property tax was being paid by the plaintiff and no objection was ever raised on behalf of the defendant.
Counsel for the plaintiff has further argued that the defendant had been allowed to occupy the suit property on license basis and his possession thereon was purely permissive.
The said license was terminated by the plaintiff through legal notice dated 15.06.2012.
Thus, the present case has been filed well within the period of limitation.
